seo.description: Quartz vs granite countertop for a Gurgaon kitchen? Compare cost per sq ft, heat and stain resistance, upkeep and which one suits Indian cooking.

title: Quartz vs Granite Countertops for Gurgaon Kitchens: Cost, Durability & Maintenance Compared
author: Shivam Kumar

featuredImage.alt: Quartz vs granite countertop comparison in a modern Gurgaon kitchen

excerpt: Quartz vs granite countertop for a Gurgaon kitchen? Compare cost per sq ft, heat and stain resistance, upkeep and which one suits Indian cooking.
keyTakeaways: Granite Handles Heat, Quartz Handles Stains — Granite tolerates hot vessels well; quartz's resin scorches above about 150°C but resists oil and turmeric without sealing.
Granite Costs Less for Common Varieties — ₹65-200 per sq ft vs ₹180-600+ for quartz, though premium granite overlaps mid-range quartz.
Sealing Is Granite's Ongoing Task — About once a year, more often for light colours; quartz never needs it.
Sunlight Rules Out Quartz Outdoors — UV exposure discolours quartz and breaks down its resin, so granite suits balconies and sun-facing counters.
Many Large Homes Use Both — Quartz in the show kitchen and island, granite in the working kitchen where the heavy cooking happens.
contentHtml:
Choose granite if you cook heavily, place hot vessels on the counter and want the lower price. Choose quartz if you want a uniform, light-coloured surface that never needs sealing and you are willing to use trivets. Granite handles heat better. Quartz resists stains better. Both last for decades when installed well.

The countertop is the hardest-working surface in the house. It takes hot vessels, turmeric, oil, knives and water every day, for years. In Gurgaon the choice usually comes down to two materials. This guide compares a quartz vs granite countertop on the things that decide it: cost, durability and upkeep.

Key Takeaways

  • Granite is natural stone. Quartz is engineered: ground quartz bound with resin.
  • Heat is quartz's weak point. Its resin tolerates only about 150°C.
  • Staining is granite's weak point. It is porous and needs sealing about once a year.
  • At Delhi NCR supplier rates, common Indian granite costs less than most quartz.
  • Many large Gurgaon homes use both: quartz where it shows, granite where the cooking happens.

Quartz vs Granite at a Glance

FactorQuartzGranite
What it isEngineered slab, about 90% or more ground quartz with resin and pigmentNatural stone, cut from quarried blocks
LookUniform colour and pattern; whites and marble looks availableEvery slab is different; strongest in blacks, browns and greys
HeatResin tolerates about 150°C; hot vessels can scorch itHandles hot cookware well
StainsNon-porous; resists oil and turmericPorous; resists stains only when sealed
ScratchesVery hard, about 7 on the Mohs scaleVery hard; natural fissures can chip at edges
SealingNot neededAbout once a year; light colours more often
Direct sunlightCan discolour; not for outdoor countersUnaffected; suits balconies and utility areas
JointsConsistent slabs, so joints matchColour varies, so select and mark your slabs
PriceHigher for most gradesLower for common Indian varieties

What Each Material Actually Is

Granite is an igneous rock, quarried in blocks and sawn into slabs. India is a major producer, so varieties such as Absolute Black, Black Galaxy, Tan Brown and Steel Grey are widely available and well priced. No two slabs match exactly.

Quartz countertops are manufactured. Ground quartz, typically 90 to 93 percent by weight, is mixed with polyester resin and pigment and pressed into slabs. The process gives consistent colour, a non-porous surface and whites that natural granite rarely offers. The resin is also the reason quartz is sensitive to heat and sunlight.

Cost: Quartz vs Granite in Gurgaon

These are rates published by stone suppliers in Delhi and elsewhere in India for 2026. They exclude GST, transport and wastage, and they are not an Omega quotation.

Material and gradeMaterial rate per sq ft30 sq ft counter, with fabrication
Granite, common Indian varieties₹65 to ₹200₹3,150 to ₹8,400
Quartz, entry level₹180 to ₹300₹6,900 to ₹13,500
Quartz, mid range₹300 to ₹600₹10,500 to ₹22,500
Quartz, premium and imported₹600 to ₹1,500+₹19,500 to ₹49,500+

Premium and imported granites cost more. One Delhi supplier lists granite up to ₹800 per sq ft, so the top of the granite range overlaps mid-range quartz.

The slab is only part of the bill. Suppliers quote these extras separately:

  • Fabrication and installation: ₹40 to ₹80 per sq ft for granite, ₹50 to ₹150 for quartz.
  • Edge profiles: a square edge is usually included. Bullnose, bevelled or waterfall edges add ₹80 to ₹200 per running foot.
  • Cut-outs: ₹800 to ₹2,000 each for the sink and hob.

For where the countertop sits in the full kitchen budget, see our modular kitchen cost guide for Gurgaon.

Durability Under Indian Cooking

Heat

This is the clearest difference. The resin in quartz withstands only about 150°C, and manufacturers describe quartz as heat resistant, not heat proof. A kadhai, tawa or pressure cooker straight off the flame is far hotter than that and can leave a brown or yellow scorch mark that is not always repairable. Granite tolerates hot cookware much better. Sudden thermal shock can crack any stone, so a trivet is still good practice on both.

Stains

Quartz is non-porous, so oil, turmeric and tamarind sit on the surface and wipe off. Granite is porous. Sealed properly it resists the same spills, but once the sealer wears off, oil and haldi can soak in, and light granites show it first. On white surfaces of either material, wipe turmeric promptly.

Scratches and chips

Both are hard enough for daily kitchen use. Quartz rates about 7 on the Mohs scale and has no natural fissures, so it is consistent edge to edge. Granite is comparably hard, but natural fissures can chip at exposed edges and around cut-outs. Use a chopping board on both. Knives lose that contest before the stone does.

Maintenance: What Each One Asks of You

TaskQuartzGranite
Daily cleaningMild soap and waterMild soap and water
SealingNoneAbout every 12 months; light granites every 6 to 9 months
Hot vesselsAlways use a trivetTrivet recommended
Harsh cleanersAvoid; they can dull the resinAvoid; they strip the sealer
RepairsScorch marks are hard to fixChips can be filled; surface can be re-polished

A simple test tells you when granite needs sealing. Leave a few drops of water on the surface. If the stone darkens within a few minutes, it is absorbing water and it is time to reseal.

What Changes in a Gurgaon Kitchen

Water

Municipal supply in Gurugram has been measured at a moderate 250 to 300 ppm TDS, but borewell water in parts of the district runs far higher. Where a society depends on borewell or tanker water, white scale builds up around the sink and tap on both materials, and it shows most on dark, polished stone. Wipe the area dry and avoid acidic descalers on the countertop itself.

Sunlight

Prolonged UV exposure can discolour quartz and break down its resin, which is why it is not used outdoors. For a utility balcony counter, a barbecue ledge or a worktop under a west-facing window, granite is the safer choice. Our guide to interior materials for Gurgaon's climate covers the rest of the kitchen.

Show kitchen and working kitchen

Larger homes often have two kitchens. A sensible split is quartz for the open show kitchen and island, where looks and easy cleaning matter, and granite for the working kitchen, where the heavy cooking and hot vessels are.

Rental and investment flats

For a flat you plan to let out, granite is the forgiving option. Tenants will not always use trivets, and a polished dark granite can be re-polished between tenancies.

Which Should You Choose?

If this describes youBetter fit
Daily Indian cooking with hot kadhais and pressure cookersGranite
You want a white or marble-look kitchenQuartz
You do not want to think about sealingQuartz
Tight budget on a standard apartment kitchenGranite
Island with a waterfall edge and matched jointsQuartz
Outdoor, balcony or sun-facing counterGranite
Rental flatGranite
Show kitchen plus working kitchenBoth

Before You Order: Seven Checks

  1. See the actual slab, not a small sample, especially for granite.
  2. Confirm thickness. 18 to 20 mm is standard for kitchen counters.
  3. Fix the edge profile and its cost per running foot.
  4. Agree where joints fall. Keep them away from the sink and hob.
  5. Finalise sink and hob models first. Cut-outs are made to their dimensions.
  6. Ask how the stone will be cut. Wet cutting at the workshop controls silica dust, which is a serious health hazard for fabricators, particularly with quartz.
  7. Get the warranty in writing, for both the slab and the installation.

faqs.question: Which is better for Indian kitchens, quartz or granite?
faqs.answer: Granite suits heavy Indian cooking because it tolerates hot vessels and costs less. Quartz suits households that want a uniform, light-coloured, stain-resistant surface and will use trivets. Neither is better in every kitchen. The right choice depends on how you cook.

faqs.question: Is quartz more expensive than granite in India?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Supplier rates for 2026 put common Indian granite at about ₹65 to ₹200 per sq ft and quartz at about ₹180 to ₹600 for entry and mid-range grades. Premium granite and imported quartz both cost considerably more.

faqs.question: Can I put a hot pan on a quartz countertop?
faqs.answer: No. The resin in quartz withstands only about 150°C, and a vessel straight off the flame can leave a permanent brown or yellow scorch mark. Always use a trivet or hot pad on quartz.

faqs.question: Does granite need to be sealed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Granite is porous, so it is sealed at installation and resealed about once a year. Light-coloured granites may need it every 6 to 9 months. If water darkens the surface within a few minutes, it is time to reseal.

faqs.question: Which lasts longer, quartz or granite?
faqs.answer: Both can last for decades. Granite's risks are staining when unsealed and chipping at edges. Quartz's risks are heat marks and discolouration in direct sunlight. Good installation and basic care matter more than the material.

faqs.question: Does turmeric stain quartz or granite?
faqs.answer: Quartz is non-porous and resists turmeric well, though it is best wiped quickly on white surfaces. Sealed granite also resists it. Unsealed or poorly sealed granite can absorb turmeric and oil, and light colours show it most.

faqs.question: What thickness is best for a kitchen countertop?
faqs.answer: 18 to 20 mm is the standard for kitchen counters in India in both materials. Thicker slabs of 25 to 30 mm, or a built-up edge, are used for islands and waterfall sides.
